'On and after' fixes an effective date; it does not create a standing guarantee of access. The order lifted a wartime closure, and the street's use then reverted to ordinary District and federal law. That is a spent one-time act (TC07; EO 12282 lesson). There is no ending instrument, and none is needed. Any present restriction on East Executive Avenue rests on other authority; I did not locate it, and it is not needed for NO. ledger_title: Executive Order No.    Exemption of Certain Officers of the Executive Branch of the Government From Compulsory Retirement for Age
review_problems: Text: I re-downloaded the NARA image (naId 284839167, object 23812613-14-001.jpg): byte-identical (sha256 807c388d...). It is a one-page White House press release (#858, Sept. 19, 1946) carrying the full order (preamble, operative clause, nine names, typed signature and date). I compared the producer's transcription word for word with the image: it matches exactly (the image shows a NARA stamp and archival page number '421', not part of the text). Grade: the producer's 'hosted_transcript' is acceptable and conservative; more precisely it is a reviewer-verified transcription of an official contemporaneous press release image, not the signed original. Correction 1: the producer says the FR shows 'identity and date only'; in fact the FR filing note at 11 FR 10645 (F.R. Doc. 46-17078, re-fetched, byte-identical) lists all nine officers, independently confirming the operative object (it misprints Draper's agency as Federal Trade Commission; the release says Federal Power Commission). The term-bound wording appears only in the release. Correction 2 (cosmetic): the govinfo OCR of 92 Stat. 191 prints the heading as 'SEC. 6.'; the U.S. Code note confirms it is sec. 5(c), as the producer says. Law: the order has ONE operative clause (the exemption); recitals carry no command. It is bounded by each officer's 1946 appointment/term (all statutory terms of these offices were 12 years or less, so every term ended by 1958 at the latest; EO 9963's further exemption for Hill confirms the bound operated). Independently, Pub. L. 95-256 sec. 5(c) struck 5 U.S.C. 8335(a)-(e) (general age-70 automatic separation and the general presidential exemption power) effective 1978-09-30; the remaining automatic-separation categories (ATC, LEO/firefighters, Alaska RR/Canal Zone) do not include any office named. So the 1978 reasoning reaches the only clause. No status conferred; any-effect no. FR API: no reference.
what_remains_inferential: Text is the producer's visual transcription of the White House press release (not printed in FR). Individual term end dates not retrieved; Tax Court judges now have their own retirement statute (26 U.S.C. 7447, not retrieved), which is not the regime exempted from.

ledger_title: Executive Order No.    Terminating the Office of Alien Property Custodian and Transferring its Function to the Attorney General
review_problems: None. The order rested in part on the First War Powers Act, whose Title I functions revert on termination (55 Stat. 838; re-read). The ending instrument, Reorganization Plan No. 1 of 1947 sec. 101(a) (61 Stat. 951; read in the Statutes at Large), transfers 'all functions vested by law in the Alien Property Custodian' to the Attorney General. So the Attorney General's holding rested on the plan, which has statutory force, from 1947-07-01. Para. 4 is a spent supersession. ledger_title: Executive Order No.   Providing for the Transfer of Properties and Personnel to the Atomic Energy Commission
review_problems: None. I re-fetched the order and mapped all ten paragraphs: - transfers (paras. 1-2, 4, 6(a)): completed; - paras. 3, 5, 6(b), 7, 8 and 9: their actor is the AEC. The ending instrument, 42 U.S.C. 5814(a) (Energy Reorganization Act 1974 sec. 104; 2024 ed.), was re-read: 'The Atomic Energy Commission is hereby abolished.' The functions went to ERDA and NRC by statute, so present DOE/NRC holdings rest on statute (TC08). Para. 8 (EO 9001 contract powers) is limited to contracts made before 1947.
